newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia '96 cocoa output seen down to 122,000t.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia '96 cocoa output seen down to 122,000t.

text.p: Malaysia's cocoa output is expected to shrink by 7.2 percent to 122,000 tonnes this year from the 131,475 tonnes produced in 1995, the Finance Ministry said on Friday in its annual economic report.

Relatively low prices, poor weather and shrinking hectarage were reasons for the lower production, said the report, which still ranked Malaysia as the sixth largest producer of cocoa in the world for 1996.
The Malaysian Cocoa Board has also forecast a production of 122,000 tonnes this year but growers polled by Reuters recently were only confident of a volume around 100,000 tonnes.
The Finance Ministry report said export revenues from cocoa beans were expected to fall 7.0 percent in 1996 to 160 million ringgit ($64 million) from 172 million ringgit in 1995.
It said the total area under cocoa in 1996 was envisaged to decline 3.3 percent to 235,000 hectares.

"Close to 95 percent of the cocoa holdings in the country are matured and many of these holdings are faced with declining yield," said the report, adding that some 2,000 hectares have been identified for rehabilitation. ($1 = 2.50 ringgit)
